newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Strong oil prices, dollar to hit Dutch gas users.
newsitem.headline: Strong oil prices, dollar to hit Dutch gas users.

text.p: Dutch gas consumers will face heftier bills in the next six months after sharp rises in oil prices and the dollar, a spokesman for the energy distributors' association said on Wednesday.
"(Total energy) bills will be about 10 percent higher," said EnergieNed spokesman Sjoerd Marbus.
Gasunie, the monopoly gas marketer and distributor will charge individual supply companies an extra 2.6 cents per cubic metre, a direct result of oil and dollar strength.
"It's about 75 percent due to oil and 25 percent due to the stronger dollar," said Marbus.

The price hike, most of which is expected to be passed on to consumers, will affect almost all energy users as gas makes up almost 45 percent of total Dutch energy consumption. Oil's share is just under 40 percent.
The Dutch government has, since the discovery in 1959 of large gas reserves, linked the price of gas to that of oil.
To make matters worse for Dutch fuel burners, the Dutch government, in its efforts to encourage energy saving, will add an energy tax of 3.2 cents per cubic metre from January.
Including value added tax, the price will rise by 6.8 cents per cubic metre.
"For the average consumer, the bill will rise by 100 guilders per year," said EnergyNed's Marbus.
